memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"The whole community of Israel must celebrate it. A foreigner residing among you
who wants to celebrate the LORD's Passover must have all the males in his
household circumcised; then he may take part like one born in the land. No
uncircumcised male may eat it. The same law applies both to the native-born and
to the foreigner residing among you." - Ex 12:47-49 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is the door standing open, spelled out plainly. A foreigner who wants to
celebrate Passover may do so. And when he does, he takes part "like one born in
the land."

Not as a second-class participant. Not in a separate section. Like one born in
the land. The same law for both.

Set this beside our tendency to rank people in church life. The long-time member
and the newcomer. The one from a Christian family and the one who came to faith
last year. The educated and the uneducated. Scripture flattens these
distinctions. James warns sharply against showing favouritism in the assembly
(Jas 2:1-4).

Paul makes the point unmistakable: "There is neither Jew nor Gentile, neither
slave nor free, nor is there male and female, for you are all one in Christ
Jesus" (Gal 3:28).

Notice the requirement, though. The foreigner had to come in through the
covenant sign. God's welcome is wide, but it is not vague. Jesus said, "I am the
way and the truth and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me"
(John 14:6). One door, open to everyone.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you treat any believer as less than "one born in the land"?
2. Have you come in through the one door God has provided?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You that Your welcome is for everyone who comes through Jesus.
Root out any favouritism in my heart. Amen.
